features.details: Ghostty-accurate VT handling, hard line breaks preserved through reflow and safe resizing while viewing scrollback, true color, minimum text contrast of 3 by default (Ghostty `minimum-contrast` from 1 to 21; 1 disables adjustment), readable text even when a running agent retains its prompt background across a theme change, wide glyphs, IME input, mouse selection and reporting, scrollback search (`cmd-f`), cmd-click links and file paths, including unquoted explicit paths with spaces or parentheses, quoted paths, and paths after a note such as `(see …)`, across soft-wrapped rows. The longest existing path wins over a shorter existing prefix; hard newlines and adjacent explicit paths stay separate. Overlong candidate searches leave the path unresolved. Hover, click and path menus share the target, and a deleted target is not replaced when activated, right-click actions on paths (reveal in Finder, open a tab or `cd` there, copy), drag and drop paths, inline images (Kitty graphics protocol), Mermaid diagrams in agent output rendered offline ("View diagram"), Markdown files previewed in the browser (right-click a `.md` path, or "Preview Markdown" in the palette), font size shortcuts, prompt jumping (`cmd-up` / `cmd-down`) Right-click a terminal selection for Copy for sharing: review and edit a plain-text preview before copying. It uses only uniquely matched assistant text from the selected pane’s exact conversation; partial selections stay partial and ambiguous selections remain unchanged. Confirmed Claude Code 2.1.296 and Codex 0.162.1 layouts restore indentation in uniquely matched code and text subsections, including Claude nested hyphen lists, while retaining confirmed older gutter layouts. Hidden code-fence delimiters and the rest of an answer are never added. Duplicate matches, incomplete transcripts and transformed tables, quotes or bullets that cannot correspond exactly keep the original selection. Ordinary Copy keeps the existing terminal selection behavior. Changed conversations block copying; cancelling restores typing focus. Linux also resolves the foreground directory through /proc when shell directory reports are unavailable. On Linux, Ctrl+Shift+C/V copy and paste, Ctrl+Shift+F opens search, and Ctrl+click follows paths and links. Ordinary Ctrl+C and other shell controls still reach the foreground process.
features.title: Ghostty inside
features.summary: True color, Unicode, IME, search, reliable scrollback resizing, your Ghostty font and colors, and readable prompt text across theme changes. Follow links and space-containing paths across wrapped rows, show Kitty graphics, and preview Mermaid diagrams and Markdown offline. Review and edit selected agent text before copying it for sharing.

features.details: Open another window with cmd-shift-n. Windows, terminal, Git tree and Diff review tabs, splits, active focus, directories and exact supported agent conversations come back after restart. A window that was in native full screen reopens at its last windowed size. Drag a tab onto another to reorder the tab bar; the order is saved and restored. Right-click a tab or a Sessions row, or use the palette, to move a running pane to a new tab, beside the pane of another tab, or to another or a new window: its process, scrollback, agent status, child activity and conversation stay with it, and a tab left empty closes without asking. Agent conversations resume in the latest directory confirmed for that exact conversation, then the captured launch or transcript directory; a missing confirmed directory keeps an error pane without resuming elsewhere. Previous working activity remains available separately from new runtime output. Only actual terminal output and delivered input update activity; theme, resize, selection, search and scroll changes keep quiet panes quiet. Every tab has a visible close button, including long labels and inactive tabs; cmd-w closes the focused pane. Working or waiting agents, and idle parents with working, waiting or unknown children, ask before stopping. Cancel is the default; Tab selects the other button and Enter or Space activates it. When a shell exits (exit or ctrl-d), its pane closes like cmd-w, whatever its exit code. A program chda started, such as a managed agent or a `[[commands]]` tab, closes the same way when it succeeds; a failure keeps its pane with the exit status, read-only output and Start shell. Closing the shown tab, with exit, its close button or cmd-w, shows another tab of the same branch, or else no tab: the window stays on that branch, the sidebar keeps it selected, and + at the end of the tab bar or cmd-t opens a new terminal there. A window stays open when its last tab closes; cmd-w on a window without tabs closes it. Linux uses Ctrl+Shift+T/W for tabs, Ctrl+Shift+D/E for splits and Alt+1 through Alt+9 to select tabs.
features.title: Keep your place, close safely
features.summary: Reorder tabs and move a running pane between tabs or windows without losing its process or scrollback. Restore layouts and supported conversations after restarting. Close a pane or a whole tab with checks for active agents.

features.details: In a configured, signed macOS release, click Update to download, verify and install with Sparkle. Progress is shared across windows; installation waits for current repository tasks and unfinished input before preserving sessions. macOS asks for administrator approval when required. Windows briefly reopen while running shells and agents, terminal text and scrollback, pane IDs, layouts and focus reconnect. Failed installation or startup reopens the retained signed app with the same sessions. Terminals that have used inline images block the update without stopping their processes. Release notes and version dismissal remain separate; automatic downloads and installs are off. v0.1.19 requires one manual update first. Linux offers the latest stable Linux package as a manual download. It does not offer a macOS-only release or stop running shells while opening the download page.
features.title: Update without stopping your work
features.summary: Click Update in the signed macOS app. Running shells and agents reconnect with their text, scrollback and window layouts. Installation failure reopens the retained app with your sessions; inline-image terminals ask you to close them first.

features.details: The focused pane's repository and branch-note alias appear as repo - task; the branch is the fallback. Custom tab names remain on tabs without hiding the repository context. Hover for the repository, full note, branch and worktree path. Open the focused worktree in a chosen installed editor or Finder. Linux discovers installed folder-capable desktop applications and available icons, and opens the selected folder through gio; the default file manager uses xdg-open. Linux has a Commands button and draws minimize, maximize and close controls plus resize edges when the compositor does not provide window decorations.
features.title: The task in the title
features.summary: See the repository and focused branch task together. Hover for the full context or open the worktree in your favorite editor.

features.title: Keep operational messages in view
features.summary: Open the title-bar bell icon for timestamped messages, unread arrivals and exact agent-pane links. Closing the list returns typing focus without deleting history.
features.details: The title-bar notification control stays immediately before the installed-app picker, even with the sidebar hidden or no available picker. Window-local history lists severity, date and UTC time, message and known directory/tab/pane context newest first. Opening reads only existing arrivals; later arrivals remain unread. Selecting an agent event goes to its exact still-open pane. Operational errors and successes no longer overwrite a single sidebar message; an ongoing branch update changes one entry. OS notifications and provider usage controls remain available. Programs can ask for a notification with OSC 9 or OSC 777, as Ghostty, iTerm2 and kitty support: the request adds an entry with its pane, marks the tab and, when the pane is out of view, sends an OS notification that focuses that pane. Text is shown plain and truncated, each pane is limited to one a second, panes with a live agent rely on its own notifications, and the notifications setting turns these off too. History retains at most 500 entries and reports removed older entries. Normal restart clears it; session-preserving updates retain each window's history and read state. On Linux, desktop notifications use the session D-Bus service; clicking one returns to its exact pane. Delivery runs off the UI thread, and a missing notification service does not block terminal input. Linux does not show a launcher badge or play a separate terminal alert sound.

Repositories and plain folders, worktrees, dirty / ahead / behind / conflict badges, lines added and removed against the default branch (click for a read-only diff tab), pull request state via `gh`, `glab` or `tea`, and open-tab counts. Two peer sections, Sessions and PROJECT, each have a header outside their own scrolling list; the wheel or trackpad moves only the list under the pointer. Sessions has one row per agent pane, so agents in split panes each get a row, with nonshrinking #1, #2 numbers when they share a tab; labels and provider names give way before the number; one row per Git tree or diff review tab; and ordinary terminal tabs last, all in tab and pane order. Rows never move when an agent starts working, waits, finishes or goes idle, and a live idle agent is listed once. Each row shows its repository and branch, or the branch note with the Alias / Branch toggle, what it is, time since the last terminal activity and a status icon whose tooltip names the state: Working, Waiting for input, Turn complete, Idle, No live agent, Terminal, Git tree or Diff review. Every ordinary terminal tab and agent pane keeps a close control; clicking it checks the latest parent and child activity before applying close confirmation. Sessions grows with its rows up to 40% of the sidebar and then scrolls, takes the remaining height when PROJECT is collapsed and shows No open sessions when empty. Clicking a session, switching tabs or panes and jumping to an agent focus the exact pane and highlight its branch in PROJECT, which scrolls only enough to reveal a clipped worktree while keeping its repository name visible. That repository name stays pinned at the top of PROJECT while you scroll and works like the repository's header: click it to collapse the repository, right-click it for the repository's menu. Sessions never scrolls by itself, and a collapsed PROJECT section stays collapsed with the highlight updated. Explicit PROJECT navigation, such as a worktree or its status dot, STARRED, Go to worktree or a notification whose pane is gone, expands PROJECT when needed. PROJECT keeps the main worktree first, then branches by name, with path as a tie-breaker and detached worktrees last. Background output, status changes, transcript indexing and refreshes move neither list nor a deliberately selected branch. Both sections collapse independently, show their counts while collapsed and remember the choice across restarts; earlier ACTIVE and IDLE settings carry over as a collapsed Sessions only when both were collapsed. Every badge and header button explains itself on hover, and "+ repo" names its shortcut, cmd-shift-o. Repositories and folders, including STARRED branches, sit beneath PROJECT. Each repository header collapses its own worktrees, and one button beside "+ repo" collapses every repository while any is open and expands them all otherwise (also View > Expand All Repositories / Collapse All Repositories and the palette); the PROJECT section toggle stays separate, and each repository's state is remembered across restarts. Drag a repository header above or below another to reorder the list; a line marks where it lands, PROJECT scrolls near its edges, and the order is saved without moving folders or changing Git. Right-click a branch and choose "Add to Starred" to keep it in a STARRED list within PROJECT, per repository and saved across restarts. Click a branch in PROJECT or STARRED to open it, reusing its most recently focused pane across windows or the configured default action; a double or triple click opens it only once. Right-click either list for Open terminal or explicit agent actions. A missing STARRED worktree stays selectable and never creates a terminal or worktree. Click its star to unstar it without leaving the current tab. If the system cannot open the folder picker for Add repository, chda keeps running with terminals, typed input and settings unchanged, records one error in the title-bar notifications, and you can try again or drop the folder on the sidebar. A working agent shows a spinning ring, an agent waiting for input an orange "!" badge on a tinted row, a finished turn a green dot, a live idle agent a yellow dot and a row with no live agent a gray dot. On light themes, or wherever a color would fade into the sidebar or tab bar, it deepens or lightens within its hue so every status icon keeps at least 3:1 contrast, selected rows included. Stars and Git badges retain their hues and at least 3:1 contrast on normal, selected and waiting rows in light and dark themes; diff counts keep at least 4.5:1. Pull request badge colors remain the same. Context menus close existing hover hints and keep hints hidden until the menu closes. A section toggle updates the next Expand or Collapse hint. Star, Refresh and other actions that keep the current pane return keyboard input there; opening a terminal or review keeps focus at the destination.
features.title: Live sessions at a glance
features.summary: Open a branch with one click, or choose a menu action for a new terminal or an agent. Stable branch order, visible split numbers and readable marks keep Sessions and PROJECT clear while agents work.

features.details: Create from a new or existing branch, delete with a safety check, merge-and-clean, bulk cleanup of merged branches, update a branch from its upstream when it is clean and no agent works in it (fast-forward; a diverged branch asks before a rebase or merge and never rewrites pushed commits); a note per branch saying what the task is (right-click "Edit note...", or `chda note <text>` inside the worktree), shown as the row's label and searchable in the palette Creation and note forms share labeled fields, a multiline note area, readable destination/context, explicit Cancel/Create/Save buttons and busy/error feedback. Cmd-V and Edit > Paste insert at the caret or replace selected text, including Unicode notes; single-line branch input flattens line breaks without submitting. Worktree preparation in the repository menu starts with empty command and file lists. Save ordered commands and explicit relative paths without executing them. First or changed plans show the actual new working directory, source/destination paths and steps for confirmation; imported settings never grant permission. Only untracked gitignored regular files are copied, through directory handles that reject symlinks and path traversal. Copies are independent and never overwrite existing files. Setup runs off the UI thread in the configured shell, after copying, with stage and exit feedback. Cancel stops owned preparation processes; failures keep the worktree and copied files. Review retry keeps existing regular files and reruns commands from the beginning, or explicitly Skip. Successful background preparation leaves tabs and typing focus alone; Open starts the planned terminal or the existing per-launch agent options. Setup in the title bar reopens hidden runs. Other windows and MCP requests cannot bypass outstanding preparation. Unfinished runs and editors defer session-preserving updates. The Setup menu opens below its badge and stays inside small windows. A rejected copy entry names the relative file and whether it is missing, tracked, not gitignored, a directory or nonregular file, a symlink, or a path outside the source root. View diff keeps UTF-8 file names readable in both the summary and patch headers while retaining the existing pager and base.
features.title: One worktree per task
features.summary: Create from any branch, label it with a note, read its diff, update from upstream, then merge and clean up with checks for unsaved or unpushed work. Opt in to selected local-file copies and ordered setup commands before opening a new worktree.

features.details: Right-click a repository and choose "View Git tree" for a read-only commit graph with parent connections, subjects, short hashes and local / remote branches, tags and HEAD. History loads in pages as you scroll; refresh or retry without opening a shell. One graph tab per repository; graph tabs restore after a restart.
features.title: Read the Git tree
features.summary: Choose View Git tree from the repository menu for commit connections, subjects, short hashes and branch, tag and HEAD labels. Browse in a read-only tab, refresh and restore it after restarting.

features.title: Review changes with private notes
features.summary: Choose Review diff from a worktree menu. Select old or new lines, add private notes and preview a batch for an exact live agent conversation. Copy and focus its pane, then paste when ready.
features.details: One native review tab per worktree keeps the existing diff pager available. Browse a unified diff with old/new line numbers and a file list that collapses in narrow windows; Shift-click selects a range within one hunk. Add, edit and resolve local notes. Exact unchanged context reconnects after refresh; missing or ambiguous locations stay Stale and require explicit reattachment. Renames keep both path identities; binary and metadata-only changes have no text anchors. Notes persist privately across restarts; failed saves keep editable drafts. Send review notes previews selected notes against a freshly read diff, including original locations for stale notes. Choose an exact live provider/conversation in the same Git worktree. Copy and go to agent rechecks the diff, notes and target, copies plain text and focuses its pane. Paste manually; direct delivery is unavailable. Working and approval-waiting input is never cleared, pasted into or automatically submitted. Copying does not resolve notes or claim delivery; changed conversations block the copy. Open editors and previews defer session-preserving updates.

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode status from their own hooks on tabs, the Sessions list, worktree rows and the Dock badge; notifications that open the agent's pane; jump to the agent that waits (`cmd-shift-a`); session list ordered by the last message, with token usage and one-click resume; Codex saved conversations remain available in the resume list with accurate user-message counts; cmd-click several sessions to resume them side by side in one tab; managed Claude Code and Codex launches show Use CLI configuration (the default) or explicit Bypass before starting, including presets, selected conversations and worktree default actions. Codex Bypass disables approvals and sandboxing. Codex launched from chda's menu or typed in its shells stays in its pane without Codex's shared background server and starts without warning about it. Conflicting preset permission options stop the launch without rewriting the preset. Captured executable, working directory, options and permission choice follow the exact conversation on resume and restore; inherited effective policy is shown as unobserved. A managed agent that exits successfully closes its pane; when it fails, its pane shows the exit state and retains the last run as read-only Previous run output; agents that return to a surviving shell keep that same shell. An exact managed-agent restart uses the same pane, confirmed conversation directory, executable, options, permission choice and exact verified conversation; repeated clicks start one successor. Missing executable, directory or transcript produces an error instead of a fresh conversation. A provider without verifiable local transcripts explains that exact resume is unavailable. Live turn completion and commands typed directly in a surviving shell do not offer restart. Stopped panes and previous output survive cold restart and session-preserving updates; available account reports are retained as reports, with CLI authentication inherited. Provider-confirmed Claude and Codex children show on their exact parent's Sessions row, also after the parent becomes idle, as small counts with icons: working, waiting for input in the waiting color, unknown and all children, with no extra line. Hover names the agent and the counts; right-click lists each child with its label, state and report age, and choosing one opens only its exact known dedicated pane or else its status details. Agent rows show the agent's short label in its color, such as CC or CX. Claude child hooks omit prompts and answers; Codex queries the existing local CLI daemon through its WebSocket byte proxy with exact parent IDs and metadata only. Unavailable or unloaded runtime state remains unknown without replacing a reported turn completion or end, and unknown children are counted separately. Codex does not report a running child's live status to chda, so such a child shows unknown. Older CLIs retain their existing top-level behavior. Children do not add usage a second time. Cold restart clears child activity; session-preserving updates retain the reports. On the launch sheet, Up and Down select the permission policy; Tab and Shift-Tab move between editable permission groups, Cancel and Start. Enter or Space activates the focused button. Cancelling returns input to the original pane; confirmation keys are consumed by the sheet. Through chda mcp, agents list their repository's sessions, read a shell's output or another agent's latest answer, and wait for a reported state across windows without moving focus or stopping live sessions. Requests observe preceding hook updates.
features.title: Agents you can see
features.summary: Track Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and OpenCode. Choose permissions per launch, resume exact supported conversations and retain failed output. See child activity as compact counts on the parent row; right-click for details. Codex starts in its pane without the shared background server warning.

features.title: Quota and local session resources
features.summary: See Claude Code and Codex quota, clear loading and retry states, reset countdowns, and selected-pane CPU, memory and listeners. Open bottom-left details with labeled bars for each reported quota window. Claude usage updates keep other windows and their live sessions running.
features.details: The bottom bar reports provider quota, never inferred from token counts. Startup shows Waiting for usage for Claude Code and Loading for Codex. Claude readings follow the focused session's configuration folder, so a session that has not answered yet shows the same sign-in's newest reading, and the last reading per folder returns after a restart marked previous run. Empty reports preserve the same session or account's last valid reading and its actual age. Claude usage updates keep other windows and their live sessions running. All windows share reports and one Codex query loop; transient failures retry promptly, and a verified account's retained reading is labeled retrying. Authentication and installation problems have specific labels and details. Claude Code reports through a per-launch status line; Codex uses the local app-server account protocol. Details separate accounts or unknown session scopes and quota windows. On macOS, selected-pane PTY descendants supply CPU, summed RSS, listening endpoints, process count and uptime. Sampling runs off the UI thread with deadlines. See docs/status-bar.md for scopes and refresh behavior. Click either provider to open details above the bottom-left controls. Each reported quota window has a labeled 0–100% bar, value and reset time; scope, source, observed age, historical reports and errors stay distinct. Unknown data creates no bar. Content scrolls inside the window. Escape or the close button dismisses the details popup and returns typing focus to its original pane. Linux samples process resources and listening TCP or unconnected UDP sockets through /proc, including IPv6, without requiring lsof.

`cmd-shift-p`: every action, worktree, agent launch and session in one fuzzy list Settings, Ghostty config, window actions, terminal copy/paste/search, About, help links and Quit are also available from the palette. Linux opens it with Ctrl+Shift+P or the Commands button.
features.title: Every action in one place
features.summary: Press `cmd-shift-p` to find worktrees, launch or resume agents and run your own commands in a tab, split or floating terminal. Agents can use `chda mcp` to create worktrees, open tabs, read session output and wait for other agents.

features.details: Reads your Ghostty font, colors and padding; chda's own settings in one TOML file; edits apply without a restart; executable discovery uses the login-shell PATH, with a validated ~/.local/bin/claude fallback for native Claude Code installations. Live configuration reload keeps the current sidebar width while its border is being dragged; other settings still apply, and file-based width changes apply again after release. Define your own `[[commands]]`, such as lazygit, a test watcher or a dev server, and run them for the focused worktree from the palette, a worktree's menu or a shortcut, in a new tab, a split or a floating terminal; each closes when the command succeeds and keeps a failure's exit status; broken entries and clashing shortcuts are reported once while the rest load. A theme pair, `theme = light:X,dark:Y` in the Ghostty config or chda's `theme`, follows macOS Light and Dark mode in every window without a restart, including Auto at sunset; View > Select Light Theme and Select Dark Theme each preview and save one half while keeping the other.
features.title: Your terminal, your settings
features.summary: Reuse your Ghostty font, colors and padding, with a light and dark theme pair that follows macOS. Edit chda's TOML settings without restarting. Homebrew and version-manager agents are found through your login shell's PATH.
